subject.title: [Feature]: Skill Workshop — surface security scan warnings before apply + allow restoring quarantined proposals

question: Should a proposal quarantined by a failed apply-time scan be restorable to pending, and what retained findings, authorization, revision, and re-scan requirements must prevent that action from becoming a scanner bypass?
rationale: The requested API changes a security-enforced lifecycle state, so code alone cannot choose the intended operator authority and audit guarantees.

options.title: Approve guarded revise-and-retry
options.body: Show findings and allow an authorized user to reopen the proposal for revision, but keep quarantine history and require a new clean scan before it becomes applicable again.

options.title: Allow an audited manual restore
options.body: Permit an explicitly authorized restore to pending while preserving findings and forcing the normal apply-time scan, accepting a broader operator-controlled recovery path.

options.title: Keep quarantine terminal
options.body: Expose detailed findings but retain the current terminal quarantine behavior, requiring users to create a new proposal after remediation.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded revise-and-retry
recommendation.body: Show findings and allow an authorized user to reopen the proposal for revision, but keep quarantine history and require a new clean scan before it becomes applicable again.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available adjacent-history routing candidate for Skill Workshop security behavior, though direct ownership evidence is limited.
